lesson_title: 20 vs 30: The Loan That Costs 18x More
hook_text: Bank: 20%. Mashonisa: 30%. Sounds close? One is EIGHTEEN times more expensive.
clip_script: Two people offer to lend you R3 000. The bank says 20 percent. The mashonisa says 30. Read the small print out loud: the bank's is 20 percent per year. The mashonisa's is 30 percent per month. The bank's rent for a whole year: R600. The mashonisa's rent for one month: R900. In his first month you pay more than the bank asks for a whole year. Three months in, you have paid R2 700 — and if you were only paying interest, the R3 000 is still owed in full. Stretch his rate to a year: 30 times 12 is 360 percent, against the bank's 20. Never compare two rates until they wear the same time period.
visual_style: Split screen: calm bank teller stacking R600 once, versus a growing monthly pile of R900 notes that towers over it, with the per-year and per-month labels flashing red.
pacing: Slow trap setup, rapid-fire monthly charges stacking, hard-stop rule at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — grow savings and spot bad loans, no formulae needed.
